text:
- [LFST.5.6] **`event_id`** — a **deterministic** UUID stamped on **every**
  `FactAssert`, derived from the run identifier and the tier identifier the
  integrator gave the engine ([NLFC.1.2]), either of which may be absent, and the
  `FactAssert`'s `seq`. All three are replay-reproducible, so `event_id`
  reproduces on replay ([RARC.5.8.8]). The fact keeps that `event_id` for as long
  as it is in working memory. What the two identifiers mean, and whether
  they are unique, is the integrator's; with neither given, `seq` alone
  distinguishes one `event_id` from another.

  **An `event_id` means nothing outside the engine that stamped it.** It
  identifies a fact within that engine's stream and the stream's replay. A fact
  that arrives from another tier is a new `FactAssert` on the receiving engine
  and gets that engine's own `event_id`; an engine **must not** take an
  `event_id` from outside, and no `event_id` correlates two streams. A program
  that must recognise one fact on two tiers gives the fact an identifier of its
  own, in a slot the author fills and maintains ([LFST.7.2.4]).

alloy.name: lfst_5_6__seq_alone_distinguishes
alloy.note: With neither identifier given, two events at different seq carry distinct event_ids. Rests on the stamp rule and the injective derivation jointly.

alloy.name: lfst_5_6__tiers_never_share_an_event_id
alloy.note: Two tiers sharing a run carry distinct event_ids at any seq, the tier identifier being in the key. Rests on the stamp rule and the injective derivation jointly.
